raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`row_argmax`'s two-stage path (rows <= 64) and the DSpark fused markov greedy step reduce scores with `tl.max` and an equality tie-break, so a NaN score never matches its own maximum. On current main an all-NaN row makes `row_argmax` return the vocab width (131072 on a 131072-wide row) and the markov combine return `INT_MAX` -- both out of range, and the index feeds the next embedding lookup, so a NaN batch fails device-side instead of drafting token 0 like `torch.argmax`.

Mixed rows are wrong too: a NaN anywhere in the row is invisible to the max, so the kernel returns the best finite index (or an arbitrary one) where `torch.argmax` returns the first NaN.

The medium-row path (rows > 64) already reduces with `_argmax_pair`, which implements torch's NaN priority and lowest-index ties. This PR brings the two remaining reductions to the same semantics.

Revives #46433 (same fix; the author closed it during stale-PR cleanup without review, and the bug is still live on main). This is that diff ported onto current main, plus the kernel tests the original PR didn't have.

## Modifications

One commit:

- `python/sglang/kernels/ops/speculative/row_argmax.py`: `_argmax_partial_kernel` reduces each tile with a NaN-propagating max and selects NaN lanes explicitly (equality alone cannot match them); `_argmax_final_kernel` reduces the partials with `_argmax_pair`.
- `python/sglang/kernels/ops/speculative/dspark/dspark_draft_model.py`: `_markov_greedy_partial_kernel` and `_markov_greedy_combine_kernel` reduce with `_argmax_pair`, keeping padded lanes out of the result even when every valid score is NaN or `-inf`.
- `test/registered/kernels/ops/speculative/test_spec_argmax_nan_semantics.py`: new kernel tests for both files -- all-NaN rows, first-NaN-wins, NaN-beats-finite-max, all-`-inf`, exact ties, and random parity vs `torch.argmax` on both row-count paths.

Finite-input results are unchanged: the reduction is comparison-only and the tie-break order is the same as before.

## Accuracy Tests

H100 pod, unpatched (main) vs patched files loaded side by side, `torch.argmax` as ground truth:

- Before: all 8 NaN cases wrong -- all-NaN 1x131072 -> 131072, all-NaN 4x129280 -> 2020, markov all-NaN 1x152064 -> 2147483647 (`INT_MAX`), first-NaN rows -> arbitrary indices, NaN loses to the finite max. All 7 finite cases correct.
- After: 15/15 cases match `torch.argmax` exactly (NaN priority, first-NaN / lowest-tie index, padded-lane exclusion).
- The added test file passes 10/10 on the same H100 (`Ran 10 tests in 2.473s -- OK`).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

H100, CUDA-event median of 200 iters on the changed kernels (finite random inputs -- the hot path), unpatched vs patched:

| kernel | shape | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| row_argmax | 1x131072 | 38.2 us | 34.5 us |
| row_argmax | 8x131072 | 37.1 us | 34.2 us |
| row_argmax | 32x152064 | 37.3 us | 34.7 us |
| row_argmax | 64x152064 | 38.9 us | 37.6 us |
| markov greedy | 1x152064 | 48.6 us | 46.0 us |
| markov greedy | 8x152064 | 85.7 us | 86.2 us |
| markov greedy | 64x129280 | 457.1 us | 459.6 us |

No regression: one `tl.reduce` replaces the old max + where + min sequence, so the changed kernels are the same speed or slightly faster. No steady-state throughput claim -- the kernels are a small slice of the decode step.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit (ruff format, ruff check --select=F401,F821,F823,UP037, isort, codespell on the changed files).
- [x] Add unit tests (`test_spec_argmax_nan_semantics.py`, 10 tests).
- [ ] Documentation (N/A: kernel-internal semantics, no user-visible surface).
- [x] Accuracy results (above); speed N/A (see Speed Tests).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=30, stage="base-b-kernel-unit", runner_config="1-gpu-small")
+
+"""NaN-semantics parity with torch.argmax for the speculative argmax kernels.
+
+The two-stage kernels must give NaNs priority and break all ties to the
+lowest index, exactly like torch.argmax. Before the fix, an all-NaN row made
+row_argmax return the vocab width and the markov greedy step return INT_MAX
+-- both out of range, so feeding the result to the next embedding lookup is a
+device-side failure. The medium-row path (rows > 64) already reduced with
+_argmax_pair and is covered here as a regression guard.
+"""
+
+import unittest
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.speculative.dspark.dspark_draft_model import (
+    markov_greedy_step,
+    markov_greedy_step_triton,
+)
+from sglang.kernels.ops.speculative.row_argmax import row_argmax
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+DEVICE = torch.device("cuda")
+
+
+class TestRowArgmaxNanSemantics(CustomTestCase):
+    def _check(self, x):
+        out = row_argmax(x)
+        ref = x.argmax(dim=-1)
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(out, ref), f"row_argmax {out} != torch {ref}")
+        return out
+
+    def test_all_nan_row_returns_first_index(self):
+        # The pre-fix kernel returned the vocab width for these shapes.
+        for rows, width in [(1, 131072), (4, 129280), (64, 152064)]:
+            x = torch.full((rows, width), float("nan"), device=DEVICE)
+            out = row_argmax(x)
+            self.assertTrue(
+                torch.equal(out, torch.zeros_like(out)),
+                f"all-NaN rows={rows} width={width}: got {out}, want 0",
+            )
+
+    def test_first_nan_wins(self):
+        for rows in (1, 64):
+            x = torch.randn(rows, 131072, device=DEVICE)
+            x[:, 90000] = float("nan")
+            x[:, 5000] = float("nan")
+            self._check(x)
+            self.assertEqual(row_argmax(x)[0].item(), 5000)
+
+    def test_nan_beats_finite_max(self):
+        x = torch.zeros(2, 131072, device=DEVICE)
+        x[0, 100] = 1e30
+        x[0, 70000] = float("nan")
+        x[1, 70000] = 1e30
+        x[1, 50] = float("nan")
+        self.assertEqual(row_argmax(x).tolist(), [70000, 50])
+
+    def test_all_minus_inf_row(self):
+        x = torch.full((4, 129280), float("-inf"), device=DEVICE)
+        out = row_argmax(x)
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(out, torch.zeros_like(out)))
+
+    def test_matches_torch_random_and_ties(self):
+        g = torch.Generator(device=DEVICE).manual_seed(0)
+        # rows <= 64 takes the two-stage path, rows > 64 the medium path.
+        for rows, width in [
+            (1, 129280),
+            (7, 131072),
+            (64, 152064),
+            (65, 131072),
+            (100, 129280),
+        ]:
+            x = torch.randn(rows, width, generator=g, device=DEVICE)
+            self._check(x)
+        # Exact ties resolve to the lowest index.
+        x = torch.zeros(3, 131072, device=DEVICE)
+        x[:, 60000] = 5.0
+        x[:, 1234] = 5.0
+        self.assertEqual(row_argmax(x).tolist(), [1234, 1234, 1234])
+        # NaN mixed into random rows keeps parity on both paths.
+        for rows in (64, 65):
+            x = torch.randn(rows, 131072, generator=g, device=DEVICE)
+            x[::3, 77777] = float("nan")
+            self._check(x)
+
+
+class TestMarkovGreedyNanSemantics(CustomTestCase):
+    def _inputs(self, rows, vocab, rank=64, seed=0):
+        g = torch.Generator(device=DEVICE).manual_seed(seed)
+        base = torch.randn(rows, vocab, generator=g, device=DEVICE)
+        embeds = torch.randn(rows, rank, generator=g, device=DEVICE)
+        w2 = torch.randn(vocab, rank, generator=g, device=DEVICE)
+        return base, embeds, w2
+
+    def _check(self, base, embeds, w2):
+        out = markov_greedy_step_triton(
+            base_logits=base, prev_embeds=embeds, w2_weight=w2
+        )
+        ref = markov_greedy_step(base_logits=base, prev_embeds=embeds, w2_weight=w2)
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(out, ref), f"triton {out} != torch {ref}")
+        return out
+
+    def test_all_nan_base_returns_first_index(self):
+        # The pre-fix combine kernel returned INT_MAX for these shapes.
+        for rows, vocab in [(1, 152064), (4, 1000)]:
+            base = torch.full((rows, vocab), float("nan"), device=DEVICE)
+            embeds = torch.zeros(rows, 64, device=DEVICE)
+            w2 = torch.randn(vocab, 64, device=DEVICE)
+            out = markov_greedy_step_triton(
+                base_logits=base, prev_embeds=embeds, w2_weight=w2
+            )
+            self.assertTrue(
+                torch.equal(out, torch.zeros_like(out)),
+                f"all-NaN rows={rows} vocab={vocab}: got {out}, want 0",
+            )
+
+    def test_first_nan_wins(self):
+        base, embeds, w2 = self._inputs(2, 152064)
+        base[:, 90000] = float("nan")
+        base[:, 5000] = float("nan")
+        self.assertEqual(
+            markov_greedy_step_triton(
+                base_logits=base, prev_embeds=embeds, w2_weight=w2
+            ).tolist(),
+            [5000, 5000],
+        )
+
+    def test_nan_beats_finite_max(self):
+        base, embeds, w2 = self._inputs(2, 152064)
+        base[0, 100] = 1e30
+        base[0, 70000] = float("nan")
+        base[1, 70000] = 1e30
+        base[1, 50] = float("nan")
+        self.assertEqual(
+            markov_greedy_step_triton(
+                base_logits=base, prev_embeds=embeds, w2_weight=w2
+            ).tolist(),
+            [70000, 50],
+        )
+
+    def test_all_minus_inf_base(self):
+        # Padded lanes must not win even when every valid score is -inf.
+        base = torch.full((4, 1000), float("-inf"), device=DEVICE)
+        embeds = torch.zeros(4, 64, device=DEVICE)
+        w2 = torch.randn(1000, 64, device=DEVICE)
+        out = markov_greedy_step_triton(
+            base_logits=base, prev_embeds=embeds, w2_weight=w2
+        )
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(out, torch.zeros_like(out)))
+
+    def test_matches_torch_reference_random(self):
+        # vocab=1000 leaves padded lanes inside the last 256-wide tile.
+        for rows, vocab in [(1, 152064), (8, 1000), (64, 129280)]:
+            base, embeds, w2 = self._inputs(rows, vocab, seed=rows)
+            self._check(base, embeds, w2)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
